God said, "You have stayed long enough at this mountain." Where might God be calling you to move forward?
Moses told judges to hear small and great alike. How can you treat people fairly?
God carried them as a man carries his son. How has God carried you?
God says, "These forty years the Lord your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing." How has God provided for you?
God gave victory as he promised. How has God gone before you?
"You shall not fear them, for it is the Lord your God who fights for you." Where do you need this assurance?
Moses pleaded to enter the land but accepted God's answer. How do you respond when God says no?
What great nation has a god so near as the Lord is to us? How have you experienced God near?
"Take care... lest you forget the things your eyes have seen." What has God done that you must not forget?
"You will find him, if you search after him with all your heart." What would wholehearted seeking look like?
"The Lord is God; there is no other besides him." How does this shape your trust?
God reminds them, "I brought you out of the house of slavery." Why do the commands start with grace?
Which of the Ten Commandments speaks to you most right now?
God says, "Oh that they had such a heart as this always, to fear me." What does God long for in you?
"Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one. You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart." What does this look like for you?
God's words are to be on your heart and taught to your children. How do you keep God's words close?
Moses warned that when they had plenty, they might forget the Lord. How does comfort affect your faith?
When your children ask what these things mean, tell them what God has done. What would you tell them?
God chose Israel not because they were great, but because he loved them. What does this show about God's love?
God keeps covenant and steadfast love to a thousand generations. How does God's faithfulness give you hope?
"Do not be afraid... the Lord your God is in your midst." What fear do you need to bring to him?
God humbled them and let them hunger to teach them that man does not live by bread alone. What has God taught you through hardship?
God was bringing them into a good land. What good things has God given you?
"Beware lest you say in your heart, 'My power has gotten me this wealth.'" How can you remember it's God who gives?
Moses says it is not because of your righteousness that God gives you the land. Why is this humbling?
Moses reminds them of the golden calf. Why is it good to remember our failures?
Moses interceded for forty days and nights. Who could you pray for persistently?
"What does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord... to walk in all his ways, to love him?" Which do you need most?
God loves the sojourner, so love the sojourner. How can you love outsiders?
"He is your praise. He is your God, who has done for you these great things." What great things has God done for you?
Moses says, "Consider the discipline of the Lord." How has God disciplined you for your good?
The land drank rain from heaven, cared for by God. What does it mean to depend on God for your needs?
Lay up these words in your heart and soul. How can you store God's word in your heart?
God would choose a place to put his name, and there they would rejoice. Where do you go to rejoice before God?
God told them not to do whatever is right in their own eyes. Where are you tempted to make your own rules?
God warned them not to copy the worship of other nations. How can you keep your worship true?
Even if a sign comes true, do not follow other gods. How can you test what you hear against God's word?
Even close family should not lead you away from God. How do you stay faithful when loved ones disagree?
"You are a people holy to the Lord your God." What does it mean to be his treasured possession?
The tithe was eaten in celebration before the Lord. How can giving become joyful?
Every third year the tithe was shared with the Levite, foreigner, orphan and widow. Who could you share with?
God wanted there to be no poor among them. How can you help those in need?
"You shall open wide your hand to your brother." Where might you be closing your hand?
Freed servants were to be sent off generously. How does remembering God's rescue shape generosity?
The Passover remembered the night God brought them out. How do you remember God's rescue?
At the Feast of Booths, "you shall be altogether joyful." What makes you joyful in God?
Each person was to give as he was able, according to God's blessing. How has God blessed you?
"Justice, and only justice, you shall follow." How can you seek justice where you are?
Offer only the best to God. What does giving God your best look like?
The king was to read God's law all his days so his heart would not be lifted up. How does daily Scripture keep you humble?
The Lord was the Levites' inheritance. What does it mean for God to be your inheritance?
God forbade looking to fortune tellers or spirits. Where do people look for guidance instead of God?
God promised a prophet like Moses. How is Jesus that prophet?
Cities of refuge protected the innocent. How is God your refuge?
Do not move your neighbour's boundary marker. How can you respect what belongs to others?
Truth required two or three witnesses. How can you be careful not to believe accusations too quickly?
"Do not be afraid... the Lord your God is he who goes with you to fight for you." What battle are you facing?
Those who were fearful could go home, so they wouldn't discourage others. How does fear spread, and how does courage?
Even in war, they were not to destroy fruit trees. What does this show about caring for creation?
Unsolved bloodshed still needed atonement. What does this show about God's concern for every life?
God protected the rights of the unloved wife's son. What does this show about God's fairness?
"A hanged man is cursed by God." How does Paul connect this with Jesus in Galatians 3?
If you see your neighbour's lost animal, return it. How can you care for others' belongings?
Build a parapet on your roof so no one falls. How can you take care for others' safety?
A runaway slave was to be sheltered and not oppressed. How can you protect the vulnerable?
Keep your vows to God promptly. What have you promised God?
You could eat from a neighbour's field but not harvest it. What does this teach about generosity and restraint?
Pay workers on time and treat the poor with dignity. How do you treat those who work for you?
Remember you were a slave in Egypt; do not pervert justice. How does remembering your past shape kindness?
Leave the gleanings for the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow. How can you leave room for others?
"You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain." How can you treat workers fairly?
Have honest weights and measures. Where is honesty tested in your daily life?
The worshipper told the story of how God rescued his family. How would you tell your story of God's rescue?
Giving to the needy was part of worship. How does caring for others honour God?
God declared them his treasured possession. What does it mean to be God's treasure?
The words of the law were written on stones in the land. How can you keep God's word visible in your life?
"This day you have become the people of the Lord your God. You shall therefore obey." How does belonging lead to obedience?
Moses lists blessings for obedience. What blessings of God are you thankful for?
God would make them the head and not the tail. What does living under God's blessing look like?
The curses describe the cost of turning from God. What does this show about the seriousness of sin?
God says, "Your clothes have not worn out." What small ways has God cared for you?
Moses warns against a root bearing poisonous fruit. What bitterness might be growing in you?
"The secret things belong to the Lord... but the things revealed belong to us." How do you live with what you don't know?
God promises to circumcise their hearts so they love him. What does God want to change in your heart?
"The word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart." How close is God's word to you?
"Choose life... loving the Lord your God, obeying his voice and holding fast to him." What does choosing life look like today?
"Be strong and courageous... he will not leave you or forsake you." Where do you need this promise?
"It is the Lord who goes before you." What lies ahead that you need God to go before you in?
The law was to be read publicly so children would hear. How can you help children hear God's word?
Moses sings, "He is the Rock, his work is perfect." What does it mean that God is your Rock?
God found Israel in a desert land and kept him as the apple of his eye. How does God see you?
Jeshurun grew fat and forgot God. How can blessing make us forget the Giver?
God says, "See now that I, even I, am he." What does this show about God's power over all?
Moses blessed the tribes because the Lord loved his people. How does God's love show in his blessings?
"The beloved of the Lord dwells in safety." What does it mean to rest in God's love?
"The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms." How does this comfort you?
God showed Moses the land he would not enter. How do you respond when you see God's promise from a distance?
Moses died and the people wept for thirty days. How does God honour his faithful servants?
Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom. How does God continue his work through new leaders?
No prophet arose like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. How does Jesus surpass even Moses?
